stem: Which ECG feature distinguishes Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome from other forms of SVT?

options.text: The presence of a delta wave, which is a slurring at the onset of the QRS complex.
A heart rate that remains below $100$ beats per minute.
A prolonged PR interval on the resting ECG.
The absence of P-waves during sinus rhythm.

explanation: The delta wave represents ventricular pre-excitation caused by forward conduction through an accessory pathway.
rationale: Look for an abnormality that occurs right at the start of ventricular contraction.

optionExplanations.A: The delta wave represents ventricular pre-excitation caused by forward conduction through an accessory pathway.
optionExplanations.B: WPW is associated with tachycardia episodes, and the rate is typically much higher than $100$ during an event.
optionExplanations.C: WPW actually features a shortened PR interval because the accessory pathway bypasses the normal delay of the AV node.
optionExplanations.D: P-waves are present in WPW during sinus rhythm; the abnormality is in how the impulse reaches the ventricles.

source.hint: Look for an abnormality that occurs right at the start of ventricular contraction.
